# Chunk c16 - SUYU-GURecomp 35015f1 literals vs MHGU 1.4.0 disassembly

SUYU "main+X" == our vaddr X. Only the 3 blocks of the input chunk are used, each judged from the 16 instructions shown for that vaddr.

| vaddr | meaning | SUYU cite | status | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0x1000 | SUYU's literal here is a distance guard, not an address: a candidate pointer p is only accepted if it lies within 0x1000 (4 KiB) of dyn_va, so the number is a size threshold and says nothing about code at offset 0x1000. For the record, our bytes at 0x1000 are a loop head inside a function, not an entry: r3 indexes a pointer table based in lr, null slots are skipped, a record matches only when its byte +4 equals r1 and its byte +5 equals r2, then a counter byte at +6 is decremented and written back, and the loop returns to 0x1000 while r3 < r12; a decremented value below 2 leaves the loop early through 0x1044. The write-back store is printed with a PC base and a register-scaled offset (strb r4, [pc, r4, ror r0]), which fits neither a record-field store nor a stack store, so the exact store target stays unresolved. | arm_recomp.cpp:641 | SKIP | `00001000: e79e0103 ldr r0, [lr, r3, lsl #2]` / `00001028: e6ef4074 strb r4, [pc, r4, ror r0]` / `0000103c: 3affffef bcc 0x1000` |
| 0x3c00 | SUYU's literals here are the two bounds of a fixed walk (`w = 0x3c00; w < 0x3d80; w += 0x40`, so 6 iterations), i.e. scan constants, not a function entry or a table base. Our bytes at 0x3c00 are the tail of a routine whose prologue lies below 0x3c00: a PC-relative data address is built with add r1, pc, r1 from the pool word 0x0154d1e3 (yielding 0x01550df7), a call to 0x7aedcc follows, then a second literal (0x01835090, taken from 0x3c3c) is used as a displacement in a pc-relative load, the loaded pointer is bumped by 8 and stored into the first word of the object returned by that call, after which add sp, sp, #16 and pop {r4, r5, r11, pc} return. 0x3c2c..0x3c3c is an inline literal pool (0x01847e60, 0x01835098, 0x01835004, 0x0154d1e3, 0x01835090; the 0x3c34 word is pool data that the linear disassembly renders as "orreq r5, r3, r4"), so nothing at 0x3c00 is a 0x40-aligned record base and the walk cannot be reading a record array laid out from this offset. | arm_recomp.cpp:1130 | SKIP | `00003c0c: e08f1001 add r1, pc, r1` / `00003c24: e28dd010 add sp, sp, #16` / `00003c28: e8bd8830 pop {r4, r5, r11, pc}` |
| 0x3d80 | Same SUYU line as the previous row; here the literal is the exclusive upper bound (`w < 0x3d80`), so the walk body never runs with w = 0x3d80 and the offset is only an arithmetic endpoint, never a location the loop reads. Our bytes there continue an initializer for an object based in r5, in a function other than the one at 0x3c00: the incoming r0 is stored at +0, the routine 0x13efda0 is called twice, first with r0..r3 = 255,255,255,255 and then with r0..r3 = 0,0,0,0, and the two results are stored at +4 and +8; then r1 = 0x10000 and r0 = 0xffff are prepared and a halfword of r4 is stored at +20. r5 and r4 are already live when the block starts and no push appears, so 0x3d80 is mid-function code and not a 0x40-aligned record boundary. | arm_recomp.cpp:1130 | SKIP | `00003d80: e5850000 str r0, [r5, #0]` / `00003d94: eb4fb001 bl 0x13efda0` |

Note: 0x3c00 and 0x3d80 are the start and the exclusive end of the same SUYU loop, so only the start value is ever used as an offset by that walk, and both of our windows show live code plus literal-pool data (0x3c00: routine tail and the pool at 0x3c2c..0x3c3c; 0x3d80: the body of a later initializer). A 0x40-stride record array spanning this range is therefore not supported by our bytes; the two literals are loop bounds, not addresses that SUYU looks up in MHGU.
